ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Figure 1 is the emblem of the 7th International Congress on Mathematical Education (ICME), featuring two adjacent right-angled triangles in its main pattern, which together form the quadrilateral $OABC$ as shown in Figure 2. In the figure, if $AB=BC=1$ and $\angle AOB=\alpha$, then what is the value of $\tan\angle BOC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since $AB=BC=1$,\\
in the right triangle $OAB$, $\sin\alpha =\frac{AB}{OB}$,\\
therefore $OB=\frac{1}{\sin\alpha}$,\\
in the right triangle $OBC$, $\tan\angle BOC=\frac{BC}{OB}=\frac{1}{\frac{1}{\sin\alpha}}=\sin\alpha$.\\
Hence, the answer is: $\boxed{\sin\alpha}$.
